title: The voyage to Rome + the storm and shipwreck on Malta

paragraphs.text: And when it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
paragraphs.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐκρίθη τοῦ ἀποπλεῖν ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν, παρεδίδουν τόν τε Παῦλον καί τινας ἑτέρους δεσμώτας ἑκατοντάρχῃ ὀνόματι Ἰουλίῳ σπείρης Σεβαστῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de ekrithē tou apoplein hēmas eis tēn Italian, paredidoun ton te Paulon kai tinas heterous desmōtas hekatontarchē onomati Iouliō speirēs Sebastēs.

paragraphs.text: And embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail unto the places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
paragraphs.original: ἐπιβάντες δὲ πλοίῳ Ἀδραμυττηνῷ μέλλοντι πλεῖν εἰς τοὺς κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν τόπους ἀνήχθημεν ὄντος σὺν ἡμῖν Ἀριστάρχου Μακεδόνος Θεσσαλονικέως·
paragraphs.translit: epibantes de ploiō Adramyttēnō mellonti plein eis tous kata tēn Asian topous anēchthēmen ontos syn hēmin Aristarchou Makedonos Thessalonikeōs·

paragraphs.text: And the next day we touched at Sidon: and Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him leave to go unto his friends and refresh himself.
paragraphs.original: τῇ τε ἑτέρᾳ κατήχθημεν εἰς Σιδῶνα, φιλανθρώπως τε ὁ Ἰούλιος τῷ Παύλῳ χρησάμενος ἐπέτρεψεν πρὸς τοὺς φίλους πορευθέντι ἐπιμελείας τυχεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: tē te hetera katēchthēmen eis Sidōna, philanthrōpōs te ho Ioulios tō Paulō chrēsamenos epetrepsen pros tous philous poreuthenti epimeleias tychein.

paragraphs.text: And putting to sea from thence, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
paragraphs.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀναχθέντες ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κύπρον διὰ τὸ τοὺς ἀνέμους εἶναι ἐναντίους,
paragraphs.translit: kakeithen anachthentes hypepleusamen tēn Kypron dia to tous anemous einai enantious,

paragraphs.text: And when we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, [a city] of Lycia.
paragraphs.original: τό τε πέλαγος τὸ κατὰ τὴν Κιλικίαν καὶ Παμφυλίαν διαπλεύσαντες κατήλθομεν εἰς Μύρα τῆς Λυκίας.
paragraphs.translit: to te pelagos to kata tēn Kilikian kai Pamphylian diapleusantes katēlthomen eis Myra tēs Lykias.

paragraphs.text: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy; and he put us therein.
paragraphs.original: κἀκεῖ εὑρὼν ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης πλοῖον Ἀλεξανδρῖνον πλέον εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν ἐνεβίβασεν ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτό.
paragraphs.translit: kakei heurōn ho hekatontarchēs ploion Alexandrinon pleon eis tēn Italian enebibasen hēmas eis auto.

paragraphs.text: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and were come with difficulty over against Cnidus, the wind not further suffering us, we sailed under the lee of Crete, over against Salmone;
paragraphs.original: ἐν ἱκαναῖς δὲ ἡμέραις βραδυπλοοῦντες καὶ μόλις γενόμενοι κατὰ τὴν Κνίδον, μὴ προσεῶντος ἡμᾶς τοῦ ἀνέμου, ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κρήτην κατὰ Σαλμώνην,
paragraphs.translit: en hikanais de hēmerais bradyploountes kai molis genomenoi kata tēn Knidon, mē proseōntos hēmas tou anemou, hypepleusamen tēn Krētēn kata Salmōnēn,

paragraphs.text: and with difficulty coasting along it we came unto a certain place called Fair Havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
paragraphs.original: μόλις τε παραλεγόμενοι αὐτὴν ἤλθομεν εἰς τόπον τινὰ καλούμενον Καλοὺς Λιμένας ᾧ ἐγγὺς ἦν πόλις Λασαία.
paragraphs.translit: molis te paralegomenoi autēn ēlthomen eis topon tina kaloumenon Kalous Limenas hō engys ēn polis Lasaia.

paragraphs.text: And when much time was spent, and the voyage was now dangerous, because the Fast was now already gone by, Paul admonished them,
paragraphs.original: Ἱκανοῦ δὲ χρόνου διαγενομένου καὶ ὄντος ἤδη ἐπισφαλοῦς τοῦ πλοὸς διὰ τὸ καὶ τὴν νηστείαν ἤδη παρεληλυθέναι, παρῄνει ὁ Παῦλος
paragraphs.translit: Hikanou de chronou diagenomenou kai ontos ēdē episphalous tou ploos dia to kai tēn nēsteian ēdē parelēlythenai, parēnei ho Paulos

paragraphs.text: and said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the lading and the ship, but also of our lives.
paragraphs.original: λέγων αὐτοῖς· Ἄνδρες, θεωρῶ ὅτι μετὰ ὕβρεως καὶ πολλῆς ζημίας οὐ μόνον τοῦ φορτίου καὶ τοῦ πλοίου ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι τὸν πλοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: legōn autois· Andres, theōrō hoti meta hybreōs kai pollēs zēmias ou monon tou phortiou kai tou ploiou alla kai tōn psychōn hēmōn mellein esesthai ton ploun.

paragraphs.text: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship, than to those things which were spoken by Paul.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης τῷ κυβερνήτῃ καὶ τῷ ναυκλήρῳ μᾶλλον ἐπείθετο ἢ τοῖς ὑπὸ Παύλου λεγομένοις.
paragraphs.translit: ho de hekatontarchēs tō kybernētē kai tō nauklērō mallon epeitheto ē tois hypo Paulou legomenois.

paragraphs.text: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to put to sea from thence, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and winter [there; which is] a haven of Crete, looking northeast and south-east.
paragraphs.original: ἀνευθέτου δὲ τοῦ λιμένος ὑπάρχοντος πρὸς παραχειμασίαν οἱ πλείονες ἔθεντο βουλὴν ἀναχθῆναι ἐκεῖθεν, εἴ πως δύναιντο καταντήσαντες εἰς Φοίνικα παραχειμάσαι, λιμένα τῆς Κρήτης βλέποντα κατὰ λίβα καὶ κατὰ χῶρον.
paragraphs.translit: aneuthetou de tou limenos hyparchontos pros paracheimasian hoi pleiones ethento boulēn anachthēnai ekeithen, ei pōs dynainto katantēsantes eis Phoinika paracheimasai, limena tēs Krētēs bleponta kata liba kai kata chōron.

paragraphs.text: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close in shore.
paragraphs.original: Ὑποπνεύσαντος δὲ νότου δόξαντες τῆς προθέσεως κεκρατηκέναι ἄραντες ἆσσον παρελέγοντο τὴν Κρήτην.
paragraphs.translit: Hypopneusantos de notou doxantes tēs protheseōs kekratēkenai arantes asson parelegonto tēn Krētēn.

paragraphs.text: But after no long time there beat down from it a tempestuous wind, which is called Euraquilo:
paragraphs.original: μετʼ οὐ πολὺ δὲ ἔβαλεν κατʼ αὐτῆς ἄνεμος τυφωνικὸς ὁ καλούμενος Εὐρακύλων·
paragraphs.translit: metʼ ou poly de ebalen katʼ autēs anemos typhōnikos ho kaloumenos Eurakylōn·

paragraphs.text: and when the ship was caught, and could not face the wind, we gave way [to it,] and were driven.
paragraphs.original: συναρπασθέντος δὲ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ μὴ δυναμένου ἀντοφθαλμεῖν τῷ ἀνέμῳ ἐπιδόντες ἐφερόμεθα.
paragraphs.translit: synarpasthentos de tou ploiou kai mē dynamenou antophthalmein tō anemō epidontes epherometha.

paragraphs.text: And running under the lee of a small island called Cauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat:
paragraphs.original: νησίον δέ τι ὑποδραμόντες καλούμενον Καῦδα ἰσχύσαμεν μόλις περικρατεῖς γενέσθαι τῆς σκάφης,
paragraphs.translit: nēsion de ti hypodramontes kaloumenon Kauda ischysamen molis perikrateis genesthai tēs skaphēs,

paragraphs.text: and when they had hoisted it up, they used helps, under-girding the ship; and, fearing lest they should be cast upon the Syrtis, they lowered the gear, and so were driven.
paragraphs.original: ἣν ἄραντες βοηθείαις ἐχρῶντο ὑποζωννύντες τὸ πλοῖον· φοβούμενοί τε μὴ εἰς τὴν Σύρτιν ἐκπέσωσιν, χαλάσαντες τὸ σκεῦος, οὕτως ἐφέροντο.
paragraphs.translit: hēn arantes boētheiais echrōnto hypozōnnyntes to ploion· phoboumenoi te mē eis tēn Syrtin ekpesōsin, chalasantes to skeuos, houtōs epheronto.

paragraphs.text: And as we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw the [the freight] overboard;
paragraphs.original: σφοδρῶς δὲ χειμαζομένων ἡμῶν τῇ ἑξῆς ἐκβολὴν ἐποιοῦντο,
paragraphs.translit: sphodrōs de cheimazomenōn hēmōn tē hexēs ekbolēn epoiounto,

paragraphs.text: and the third day they cast out with their own hands the tackling of the ship.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ αὐτόχειρες τὴν σκευὴν τοῦ πλοίου ἔρριψαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai tē tritē autocheires tēn skeuēn tou ploiou erripsan.

paragraphs.text: And when neither sun nor stars shone upon [us] for many days, and no small tempest lay on [us,] all hope that we should be saved was now taken away.
paragraphs.original: μήτε δὲ ἡλίου μήτε ἄστρων ἐπιφαινόντων ἐπὶ πλείονας ἡμέρας, χειμῶνός τε οὐκ ὀλίγου ἐπικειμένου, λοιπὸν περιῃρεῖτο ἐλπὶς πᾶσα τοῦ σῴζεσθαι ἡμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: mēte de hēliou mēte astrōn epiphainontōn epi pleionas hēmeras, cheimōnos te ouk oligou epikeimenou, loipon periēreito elpis pasa tou sōzesthai hēmas.

paragraphs.text: And when they had been long without food, then Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.
paragraphs.original: Πολλῆς τε ἀσιτίας ὑπαρχούσης τότε σταθεὶς ὁ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἔδει μέν, ὦ ἄνδρες, πειθαρχήσαντάς μοι μὴ ἀνάγεσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς Κρήτης κερδῆσαί τε τὴν ὕβριν ταύτην καὶ τὴν ζημίαν.
paragraphs.translit: Pollēs te asitias hyparchousēs tote statheis ho Paulos en mesō autōn eipen· Edei men, ō andres, peitharchēsantas moi mē anagesthai apo tēs Krētēs kerdēsai te tēn hybrin tautēn kai tēn zēmian.

paragraphs.text: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer; for there shall be no loss of life among you, but [only] of the ship.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν παραινῶ ὑμᾶς εὐθυμεῖν, ἀποβολὴ γὰρ ψυχῆς οὐδεμία ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν πλὴν τοῦ πλοίου·
paragraphs.translit: kai ta nyn parainō hymas euthymein, apobolē gar psychēs oudemia estai ex hymōn plēn tou ploiou·

paragraphs.text: For there stood by me this night an angel of the God whose I am, whom also I serve,
paragraphs.original: παρέστη γάρ μοι ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗ εἰμι, ᾧ καὶ λατρεύω, ἄγγελος
paragraphs.translit: parestē gar moi tautē tē nykti tou theou, hou eimi, hō kai latreuō, angelos

paragraphs.text: saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must stand before Caesar: and lo, God hath granted thee all them that sail with thee.
paragraphs.original: λέγων· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Παῦλε· Καίσαρί σε δεῖ παραστῆναι, καὶ ἰδοὺ κεχάρισταί σοι ὁ θεὸς πάντας τοὺς πλέοντας μετὰ σοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: legōn· Mē phobou, Paule· Kaisari se dei parastēnai, kai idou kecharistai soi ho theos pantas tous pleontas meta sou.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even so as it hath been spoken unto me.
paragraphs.original: διὸ εὐθυμεῖτε, ἄνδρες· πιστεύω γὰρ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι οὕτως ἔσται καθʼ ὃν τρόπον λελάληταί μοι.
paragraphs.translit: dio euthymeite, andres· pisteuō gar tō theō hoti houtōs estai kathʼ hon tropon lelalētai moi.

paragraphs.text: But we must be cast upon a certain island.
paragraphs.original: εἰς νῆσον δέ τινα δεῖ ἡμᾶς ἐκπεσεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: eis nēson de tina dei hēmas ekpesein.

paragraphs.text: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven to and fro in the [sea of] Adria, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some country:
paragraphs.original: Ὡς δὲ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτη νὺξ ἐγένετο διαφερομένων ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ Ἀδρίᾳ, κατὰ μέσον τῆς νυκτὸς ὑπενόουν οἱ ναῦται προσάγειν τινὰ αὐτοῖς χώραν.
paragraphs.translit: Hōs de tessareskaidekatē nyx egeneto diapheromenōn hēmōn en tō Adria, kata meson tēs nyktos hypenooun hoi nautai prosagein tina autois chōran.

paragraphs.text: and they sounded, and found twenty fathoms; and after a little space, they sounded again, and found fifteen fathoms.
paragraphs.original: καὶ βολίσαντες εὗρον ὀργυιὰς εἴκοσι, βραχὺ δὲ διαστήσαντες καὶ πάλιν βολίσαντες εὗρον ὀργυιὰς δεκαπέντε·
paragraphs.translit: kai bolisantes heuron orgyias eikosi, brachy de diastēsantes kai palin bolisantes heuron orgyias dekapente·

paragraphs.text: And fearing lest haply we should be cast ashore on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for the day.
paragraphs.original: φοβούμενοί τε μή που κατὰ τραχεῖς τόπους ἐκπέσωμεν ἐκ πρύμνης ῥίψαντες ἀγκύρας τέσσαρας ηὔχοντο ἡμέραν γενέσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: phoboumenoi te mē pou kata tracheis topous ekpesōmen ek prymnēs rhipsantes ankyras tessaras ēuchonto hēmeran genesthai.

paragraphs.text: And as the sailors were seeking to flee out of the ship, and had lowered the boat into the sea, under color as though they would lay out anchors from the foreship,
paragraphs.original: τῶν δὲ ναυτῶν ζητούντων φυγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ χαλασάντων τὴν σκάφην εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν προφάσει ὡς ἐκ πρῴρης ἀγκύρας μελλόντων ἐκτείνειν,
paragraphs.translit: tōn de nautōn zētountōn phygein ek tou ploiou kai chalasantōn tēn skaphēn eis tēn thalassan prophasei hōs ek prōrēs ankyras mellontōn ekteinein,

paragraphs.text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν ὁ Παῦλος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ καὶ τοῖς στρατιώταις· Ἐὰν μὴ οὗτοι μείνωσιν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ, ὑμεῖς σωθῆναι οὐ δύνασθε.
paragraphs.translit: eipen ho Paulos tō hekatontarchē kai tois stratiōtais· Ean mē houtoi meinōsin en tō ploiō, hymeis sōthēnai ou dynasthe.

paragraphs.text: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
paragraphs.original: τότε ἀπέκοψαν οἱ στρατιῶται τὰ σχοινία τῆς σκάφης καὶ εἴασαν αὐτὴν ἐκπεσεῖν.
paragraphs.translit: tote apekopsan hoi stratiōtai ta schoinia tēs skaphēs kai eiasan autēn ekpesein.

paragraphs.text: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take some food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.
paragraphs.original: Ἄχρι δὲ οὗ ἡμέρα ἤμελλεν γίνεσθαι παρεκάλει ὁ Παῦλος ἅπαντας μεταλαβεῖν τροφῆς λέγων· Τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτην σήμερον ἡμέραν προσδοκῶντες ἄσιτοι διατελεῖτε, μηθὲν προσλαβόμενοι·
paragraphs.translit: Achri de hou hēmera ēmellen ginesthai parekalei ho Paulos hapantas metalabein trophēs legōn· Tessareskaidekatēn sēmeron hēmeran prosdokōntes asitoi diateleite, mēthen proslabomenoi·

paragraphs.text: Wherefore I beseech you to take some food: for this is for your safety: for there shall not a hair perish from the head of any of you.
paragraphs.original: διὸ παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς μεταλαβεῖν τροφῆς, τοῦτο γὰρ πρὸς τῆς ὑμετέρας σωτηρίας ὑπάρχει· οὐδενὸς γὰρ ὑμῶν θρὶξ ἀπὸ τῆς κεφαλῆς ἀπολεῖται.
paragraphs.translit: dio parakalō hymas metalabein trophēs, touto gar pros tēs hymeteras sōtērias hyparchei· oudenos gar hymōn thrix apo tēs kephalēs apoleitai.

paragraphs.text: And when he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; and he brake it, and began to eat.
paragraphs.original: εἴπας δὲ ταῦτα καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαρίστησεν τῷ θεῷ ἐνώπιον πάντων καὶ κλάσας ἤρξατο ἐσθίειν.
paragraphs.translit: eipas de tauta kai labōn arton eucharistēsen tō theō enōpion pantōn kai klasas ērxato esthiein.

paragraphs.text: Then were they all of good cheer, and themselves also took food.
paragraphs.original: εὔθυμοι δὲ γενόμενοι πάντες καὶ αὐτοὶ προσελάβοντο τροφῆς.
paragraphs.translit: euthymoi de genomenoi pantes kai autoi proselabonto trophēs.

paragraphs.text: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
paragraphs.original: ἤμεθα δὲ αἱ πᾶσαι ψυχαὶ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ διακόσιαι ἑβδομήκοντα ἕξ.
paragraphs.translit: ēmetha de hai pasai psychai en tō ploiō diakosiai hebdomēkonta hex.

paragraphs.text: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.
paragraphs.original: κορεσθέντες δὲ τροφῆς ἐκούφιζον τὸ πλοῖον ἐκβαλλόμενοι τὸν σῖτον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν.
paragraphs.translit: koresthentes de trophēs ekouphizon to ploion ekballomenoi ton siton eis tēn thalassan.

paragraphs.text: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they perceived a certain bay with a beach, and they took counsel whether they could drive the ship upon it.
paragraphs.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἡμέρα ἐγένετο, τὴν γῆν οὐκ ἐπεγίνωσκον, κόλπον δέ τινα κατενόουν ἔχοντα αἰγιαλὸν εἰς ὃν ἐβουλεύοντο εἰ δύναιντο ἐξῶσαι τὸ πλοῖον.
paragraphs.translit: Hote de hēmera egeneto, tēn gēn ouk epeginōskon, kolpon de tina katenooun echonta aigialon eis hon ebouleuonto ei dynainto exōsai to ploion.

paragraphs.text: And casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time loosing the bands of the rudders; and hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὰς ἀγκύρας περιελόντες εἴων εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ἅμα ἀνέντες τὰς ζευκτηρίας τῶν πηδαλίων, καὶ ἐπάραντες τὸν ἀρτέμωνα τῇ πνεούσῃ κατεῖχον εἰς τὸν αἰγιαλόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai tas ankyras perielontes eiōn eis tēn thalassan, hama anentes tas zeuktērias tōn pēdaliōn, kai eparantes ton artemōna tē pneousē kateichon eis ton aigialon.

paragraphs.text: But lighting upon a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground; and the foreship struck and remained unmoveable, but the stern began to break up by the violence [of the waves].
paragraphs.original: περιπεσόντες δὲ εἰς τόπον διθάλασσον ἐπέκειλαν τὴν ναῦν, καὶ ἡ μὲν πρῷρα ἐρείσασα ἔμεινεν ἀσάλευτος, ἡ δὲ πρύμνα ἐλύετο ὑπὸ τῆς βίας.
paragraphs.translit: peripesontes de eis topon dithalasson epekeilan tēn naun, kai hē men prōra ereisasa emeinen asaleutos, hē de prymna elyeto hypo tēs bias.

paragraphs.text: And the soldiers` counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any [of them] should swim out, and escape.
paragraphs.original: τῶν δὲ στρατιωτῶν βουλὴ ἐγένετο ἵνα τοὺς δεσμώτας ἀποκτείνωσιν, μή τις ἐκκολυμβήσας διαφύγῃ·
paragraphs.translit: tōn de stratiōtōn boulē egeneto hina tous desmōtas apokteinōsin, mē tis ekkolymbēsas diaphygē·

paragraphs.text: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stayed them from their purpose; and commanded that they who could swim should cast themselves overboard, and get first to the land;
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης βουλόμενος διασῶσαι τὸν Παῦλον ἐκώλυσεν αὐτοὺς τοῦ βουλήματος, ἐκέλευσέν τε τοὺς δυναμένους κολυμβᾶν ἀπορίψαντας πρώτους ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἐξιέναι,
paragraphs.translit: ho de hekatontarchēs boulomenos diasōsai ton Paulon ekōlysen autous tou boulēmatos, ekeleusen te tous dynamenous kolymban aporipsantas prōtous epi tēn gēn exienai,

paragraphs.text: and the rest, some on planks, and some on [other] things from the ship. And so it came to pass, that they all escaped safe to the land.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς οὓς μὲν ἐπὶ σανίσιν οὓς δὲ ἐπί τινων τῶν ἀπὸ τοῦ πλοίου· καὶ οὕτως ἐγένετο πάντας διασωθῆναι ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν.
paragraphs.translit: kai tous loipous hous men epi sanisin hous de epi tinōn tōn apo tou ploiou· kai houtōs egeneto pantas diasōthēnai epi tēn gēn.
